messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]

Date of Admission: [redacted]

Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Reason for Admission:
The patient was admitted to the emergency department due to a 12-day history of cyclical fevers with vague abdominal pain.

Hospital Course:
Initial vital signs showed a blood pressure of 149/80 mmHg, a heart rate of 107 beats per minute, a temperature of 99.2ºF, a respiratory rate of 16, and a pulse oximetry reading of 100% on room air. Laboratory values showed a drop in hemoglobin and mild leukocytosis with no evidence of urinary tract infection. A computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast showed multiple liver abscesses, septic thrombophlebitis of the portal system, and evidence of ruptured appendicitis. The patient was started on broad-spectrum IV antibiotics and underwent IR-guided abscess drainage.

Treatment:
The patient was treated with IV antibiotics and underwent abscess drainage.

Condition at Discharge:
The patient's condition improved significantly after treatment.

Follow-Up:
Follow-up appointments were scheduled with the patient's primary care provider for further evaluation and treatment.

Restrictions:
The patient was advised to avoid strenuous activities until further notice.

Medications:
No medications were prescribed at the time of discharge.

Procedures:
The patient underwent IR-guided abscess drainage and interval appendectomy.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Summary:
The patient presented to the emergency department with a 12-day history of cyclical fevers with vague abdominal pain. Imaging studies revealed the presence of liver abscesses, septic thrombophlebitis of the portal system, and ruptured appendicitis. The patient was treated with IV antibiotics and underwent abscess drainage and interval appendectomy. The patient's condition improved significantly and follow-up appointments were scheduled with the primary care provider.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The ruptured appendicitis is the source of the sepsis, causing the portal septic thrombophlebitis and liver abscesses, so it is the condition chiefly responsible for the admission. Appendicitis belongs to chapter K (Diseases of the digestive system). Its three-character category is K35, acute appendicitis.

CODE: K35
